Hi Susan — thanks for the context and the export. Helpful. Short answer: we can do either, but the commercial mechanics differ. Options below — I'll summarize the business impact so procurement and the ML team can pick the best path.

Option A — 2-week time-top-up (no additional charge):
- We extend the POC by two weeks with the same token caps and SLAs.
- No additional discount; we waive a one-time administration fee for customers in this stage.
- Best if you need more wall-clock time to validate integrations and edge cases.

Option B — Credit voucher (one-time monetary credit):
- We issue a $5,000 voucher that can be applied against Hosted usage or discounted toward your first month of Dedicated.
- Voucher is invoiced as an account credit line; procurement-friendly.
- If you later convert to Dedicated within 90 days, we can stack the voucher toward the commit.

Option C — Convert unused tokens into a partial seat/commit credit:
- We can convert up to 50% of unused committed tokens into a price credit that lowers the first-month Dedicated commit by 10%. This requires a short amendment (SOW).
- This path needs approvals from my manager for margin impact.

A couple of tradeoffs: extensions delay committed revenue recognition; vouchers preserve timing but reduce billing. Seat/commit conversions complicate accounting but increase the likelihood of expansion.

If you want, I can pull a formal amendment and a quick SOW with the voucher language. Which would you prefer — extra time to test, or a procurement-friendly voucher?

Best,
